density.chosen_from: uniform over 1..4 per PLAN (the line-binding ceiling), from a stream seeded on (seed, 'density'); each line then draws its participation uniform over 1..3, and the end-rhyme pass binds free line ends on top (M-191)

end_rhyme.chosen_from: NOT A DRAW — each sung section's own `schemes[fn].rgs` re-realised at the line ends, so this consumes no seed entropy and the placement draw above is untouched. Three counts, never summed (doctrine 79): `added` groups emitted; `blocked` blocks whose ends the placement draw had already spent; `narrow` blocks whose lines cannot carry one more DISTINCT word.

meter.chosen_from: 178 derived cycles (beats envelope [2, 12], slots envelope [5, 48]), measured BY DERIVATION ON THE DECLARED COORDINATE: 1 of 11 beats-per-line values, then 1 of 3 bars x subdivision factorisation(s) of 7 beats, then 1 of 3 groupings of 7. The line runs 7 beat(s) — at most the density band's ceiling, since a sung line carries at least one syllable a beat — and holds 7 slot(s), at least the band's floor. Both ends are the same calibrated band in different units; the pair share follows from how many ways each beat count factorises. Unit is notation, never enforced

plan.title: The Last Bus Home
plan.writer_brief:
Write a song: 12 lines, 4 sections, in this order:
  [VERSE — 7 lines — 7 bars of 7/8, one-beat pickup]
      up to 6 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 1 line — 1 bar of 7/8, one-beat pickup]
      up to 6 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 1 line — 1 bar of 7/8, one-beat pickup]
      up to 6 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [OUTRO — 3 lines — 3 bars of 7/8, one-beat pickup]
      up to 6 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
Feel: 7/8 grouped 2+3+2.
Rhyme plan (line numbers over the whole song):
  lines 1.T1 & 2.T5 & 5.T5 & 7.endword stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 3 & 6.T2 stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1.T4 & 3.T1 & 4.T3 & 6.head & 7.T5 stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 10.T2 & 12.endword stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 10.head & 11.T2 stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 10.T3 & 11.T4 stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1 & 2 & 5 stand in CONSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
Story plan (one job per sung section; each enters from the section before it as stated):
  VERSE1 lets the pressure in
  CHORUS1 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — against VERSE1
  CHORUS2 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — set beside (connection unstated) CHORUS1
  OUTRO1 is the leave-taking — the walk home — after CHORUS2
Every chorus after the first repeats the first chorus word for word, line for line.
Line 8 is the hook — make it the line someone leaves humming.
Where a binding sits (a bare line number is its end word, read as a rhyme span):
  T1: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T5: word 5, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  endword: the end word, read whole, from its first syllable
  T2: word 2, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T4: word 4, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T3: word 3, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  head: the first word, its first syllable — the head-rhyme / alliteration reading
